item.title: Declining religious participation linked to rising deaths of despair
item.description: A decline in religious participation among middle-aged, less educated white Americans may have played a role in the widely noted increases in "deaths of despair," a new study finds.

item.title: Mitochondria shift toward the cell edge in response to glucose
item.description: Unlike our organs, cell organelles such as mitochondria are not fixed in place, but when, where, how, and why organelles move remain unclear.

item.title: Hidden kinase state enables rapid and repeated protein phosphorylation
item.description: Scientists at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital have characterized a hidden intermediate state at the center of Src kinase function. This hidden state allows the kinase to repeatedly modify its target, without needing to release and reattach to the target each time.

item.title: New research reveals a hidden source of cellular bioelectricity
item.description: Many biological processes are regulated by electricity-from nerve impulses to heartbeats to the movement of molecules in and out of cells.

item.title: Skin and internal organs sense cold through different molecular pathways
item.description: A research team led by Félix Viana, co-director of the Sensory Transduction and Nociception laboratory at the Institute for Neurosciences (IN), a joint research centre of the Spanish National Research Council (CSIC) and Miguel Hernández University of Elche (UMH), has demonstrated that the body uses different molecular mechanisms to detect cold in the skin and in internal organs.

item.title: People with central vision loss can accurately judge approaching vehicles
item.description: ​People with central vision loss can judge the motion of vehicles almost as accurately as people with normal vision, a new international study shows.

item.title: Simple blood test maps hidden Alzheimer’s disease changes
item.description: This population-based study used plasma pTau217 to estimate how common Alzheimer’s disease neuropathological changes are across age and cognitive status in a Norwegian community cohort. Prevalence rose steeply with age and was strongly associated with APOE ε4 genotype, education level, and kidney function, with implications for future use of blood biomarkers in clinical practice.

item.title: Simple fruit granola intervention shows promising cardio-renal signals in CKD patients
item.description: A single-arm intervention study in Japanese adults with moderate chronic kidney disease found that replacing breakfast with fruit granola for two months lowered systolic blood pressure, reduced LDL-related lipid markers, and decreased a urinary marker of tubular injury. Renal function remained stable, bowel habits improved, and findings were exploratory due to the small, open-label design.

item.title: Blood metabolite profiling outperforms BMI in predicting pregnancy complications
item.description: This study shows that a blood-based metabolomic signature linked to maternal BMI predicts gestational diabetes and preeclampsia more strongly than BMI alone, particularly in late pregnancy. A subset of 16 metabolites statistically mediates the BMI–gestational diabetes association, highlighting metabolic pathways that may improve prenatal risk stratification.

item.title: Getting a dog for the first time boosts walking and remote social ties
item.description: First-time dog owners in Japan showed significant increases in walking activity and non-face-to-face social contact over one year compared with non-dog owners. No significant changes were observed in vigorous activity or face-to-face social contact, highlighting specific behavioral associations rather than broad lifestyle shifts.
